Kil’jaeden, the Deceiver, dismisses the deaths of those he calls expendable. He boasts that he will succeed where Sargeras failed, destroy the world and secure his place as the true master of the Burning Legion. His words celebrate progress toward destruction and challenge whom his listeners can trust.

Kalecgos promises to channel power into orbs and urges heroes to strike the weakened Deceiver. Kalecgos declares love for Anveena and desperately asks her to return, believing only she can cleanse the Sunwell. In a farewell, Kalecgos credits her sacrifice with changing destiny and restoring purity, urging the heroes to honor it and describing it as hope for the future.

Twonky is one of Gearmaster Mechazod’s mechanical lieutenants, assigned to the West Point station. The airstrip assault calls for dismantling it after the station valves disrupt its work; when it appears, it starts attacking and shouts its own name.

ED-210 is one of Gearmaster Mechazod’s mechanical lieutenants, assigned to the North Point station. The airstrip assault calls for dismantling it after the station valves disrupt its work. It announces “ED-210 online!” when it appears, then starts attacking.

Max Blasto is one of Gearmaster Mechazod’s mechanical lieutenants, assigned to the Mid Point station. When it appears, it calls itself Mechazod’s herald and threatens to “dec curse” its opponents, then attacks. The airstrip assault calls for dismantling it after the station valves disrupt its work.

It threatens intruders, insisting their meddling will end and that Mechazod will relieve their curse once it is done with them. The airstrip assault calls for dismantling it after the station valves disrupt its work.

Gearmaster Mechazod offers immortality and says he only wishes to help, calling his opponents his children. When they refuse him, he mourns the conflict but threatens to kill them. His words reveal a paternal view of his targets and a coercive response to their resistance.

Sage Earth and Sky tells challengers to focus their will on the lodge totem to bring the storm, defeat it, and take its essence; the storm answers, “You will not master me, puny $r!” Its words show defiance toward the challenger, while its role is confined to the trial described in the quest.

The Fizzcrank gnome ghosts speak collectively about their encounter with Gearmaster Mechazod. They say they accidentally found and reassembled his pieces, and that he then “de-cursed” them by restoring their mechanical forms. They repeat his claim that gnomes were originally mechagnomes and that the Curse of Flesh affects Titan creations.
An ore cart associated with rail travel; its release is accompanied by a squeak.

A Frostwave Lieutenant is summoned from an ice stone as part of Ahune’s effort to enter the world. On appearing, this lieutenant declares that the Frost Lord will prevail and that the Tidehunter’s victory will freeze the land, explicitly presenting the conflict as a bid to defeat Ragnaros.

It declares that the Tidehunter will enter this world, defeat Ragnaros, and turn the land into a frozen paradise. It sees mortals as enemies of that purpose and attacks with knockdown and freezing magic.

The Image of the Lich King praises a blood prince’s progress in the region. Surprised to see Thassarian, the image says there has been no word from Mograine or the other death knights for months and asks whether Thassarian has come to rejoin the Scourge. The image orders a San’layn to return to Icecrown with a fool’s head, threatening rejection for failure.

A boar.

Lorn Deathspeaker, a humanoid.
A Horde warrior of the Sons of Warsong.
An Alliance soldier.
A humanoid necromancer of Dragonblight's carrion field.
An undead gargoyle of Dragonblight's carrion field.

During the Culling, Jaina addresses Arthas as he acts: she begins, “You can't just—” and later says she is sorry and cannot watch him do this. Her protest and apology show her opposition to his actions and distress at this moment.
Known as Wisp of Ragnaros.
A Forsaken blightcaller.
Tu’u’gwar is a beast known as “He Who Plays With Food.” Tua’kea seeks its death, prepares meat to lure it to a baited hook in the water and warns the hunter not to be swallowed whole.
Carrion Necromancer, a humanoid.
A Carrion Ghoul, an undead creature.
A Carrion Gargoyle, an undead creature.
A carrion abomination roams the hillside in the Eastern Carrion Fields. Lord Bevis describes it as an abomination on the southern hillside and makes it the target of his revenge.
Scarlet Footman, a humanoid.
An undead Scourged Scarlet Footman.

Uther the Lightbringer is a Knight of the Silver Hand who insists that Prince Arthas remains junior to him as a paladin. Uther rejects Arthas’s command, saying he would refuse even if Arthas were king. He urges another way, challenges talk of treason and warns that Arthas has crossed a terrible threshold.

Meathook is a brutish, cruel combatant who greets a fight as play and newcomers as toys. He taunts fallen opponents to get up because he is not finished with them, yet complains that the encounter is boring and dies saying it was not fun.

Salramm the Fleshcrafter is a calculating servant of a master whose plan continues beyond his own death. He welcomes the arriving champion as entertainment, regards the dead as due to have their day, and treats slain opponents as quality materials for his craft. His final words insist that his killer advances the master's plan.
The Mesmerized Frog is an ordinary frog described as entranced by sunlight reflected from Zeh'gehn's knife. It croaks eagerly while gazing toward the docked ship.

Chrono-Lord Epoch is a dragonflight-aligned enemy who confronts Prince Arthas, taunting him about his fate and challenging him in battle. His remarks about time reflect the temporal conflict surrounding the Culling of Stratholme.

Mal'Ganis is a dreadlord who claims to have been waiting for Prince Arthas. During the Culling of Stratholme, he boasts that the city's people are his and threatens to extinguish their lives household by household.
Craig Amai is a humanoid.
Zab Steambolt is identified as the Howling Fjord Zeppelin Master.
Lini Lugbolt is identified as the Borean Tundra Zeppelin Master.
Hansric Stout is identified as a dockmaster.
Maye Piper is identified as a dockmaster.
The Converted Harvest Collector is a mechanical harvest collector.
An imprisoned monkey.
A Lingering Villager is identified as a villager who lingers.
Justin's Test NPC is labeled as a test NPC.

A Drakkari warrior has watched Drak'Tharon fall to the Scourge and is terrified by the slaughter around him. His cries that the keep is lost and the Scourge are everywhere end in a bleak call for every troll to fend for themselves, showing how fear has shattered any sense of solidarity.
A hungry worg, a wild animal defined by its need to feed.
A rabbit native to Grizzly Hills, represented as a small critter rather than a service-giving character.
A ravenous worg, a wild animal. Its entry is associated with a dedicated script, though the supplied evidence does not show what that script makes it do.

A spiritual insight transformation lets a freed spirit serve as the player's eyes. The spirit says its people are dead or deranged and guides the player toward the village, asking them to watch carefully as they approach.
Grunt Tar'yug, a humanoid.
An elite Crystal Handler that casts Flash of Darkness during combat.

Ursoc is a bear god revered by the Grizzly Hills furbolgs, and Orsonn and Kodian are counted as his offspring. In the Vordrassil crisis, his spirit is tainted by the tree's dark influence and Old God power; druids seek to cleanse it. Tur Ragepaw is recruited to help confront Ursoc, whose spirit remains the concern even if his body falls.

Oacha'noa is the Goddess of the Depths, summoned through the Pearl of the Depths so the Kalu'ak can seek her augury. She is wary of the caller's possible ties to local trolls and distrusts uncertainty, requiring a display of respect before sharing guidance. Her test uses a mild compulsion to urge a leap into the water, though she leaves the final choice to the caller and is curious whether they resist; afterward, she says she has information for the Kalu'ak.
A Durnholde captain of elite standing.
A humanoid Durnholde captain.

Svala Sorrowgrave eagerly pledges service to a king and champions the Lich King’s might against enemies of the Scourge. Svala expresses delight at an unfamiliar sensation, offers to slaughter enemies in the king’s name and boasts of vanquishing souls and providing another soul for the master.
A beast called a Darkweb Hatchling that joins combat when summoned.
A summoned Anub'ar invader that attacks as it enters the fight.
The Warsong Battle Standard is a battlefield standard rather than a speaking character. It is passive.
A Statis orb.
A Ymirjar Warrior is a rank-and-file fighter among the Ymirjar. In combat, it uses Hamstring to hinder an opponent.
A Ymirjar Witch Doctor is a spellcaster among the Ymirjar. In combat, it casts Shadow Bolt.
A Ymirjar Harpooner is a ranged fighter among the Ymirjar. In combat, it uses Net to impede an opponent.
A riding kodo is an animal mount.
A Scourged Drakkari Oracle is a Drakkari oracle under the Scourge.
A Scourged Drakkari Warmonger is a Drakkari fighter under the Scourge.
A humanoid known as the Dragonblight Test Subject.

In the Brewfest plot against Coren Direbrew, Brewfest Spy serves as the camp’s informant inside the Grim Guzzler and is expected to know more about Direbrew’s scheme. He fears Direbrew will sabotage the holiday and insists that he must be stopped so Brewfest and its brews can continue.
An air elemental identified with Borean Tundra.
Ilsa Direbrew is a Dark Iron Brewmaiden, an elite figure bearing the Direbrew name.
A Direbrew minion serving as combat support.
A Sunwell daily gem vendor.
A freed giant who had been bound by a terrible runic spell and made to obey the iron dwarves. The giant voices relief and gratitude after release.
Iron Rune Avengers fight for Loken and oppose Kurun’s giants at Boulder Hills. This one calls its cause a destiny, praises Loken, and taunts those who fight Kurun’s “hopeless battle.”
Fizzcrank Bomber Escort is a mechanical escort.
Scott Keenan, known by the designation “Thug Life,” is a demon.

Commander Kolurg leads a task that is not yet complete when intruders arrive. He calls out, “Our task is not yet done!”, then challenges them with “What is this? Mok-thorin ka! Kill them!” His final recorded utterance is a pained “Gaagh...”
Horde Berserkers are elite combatants. This berserker can cast Bloodlust in battle.
Horde Rangers are elite combatants who attack at range. This ranger uses Shoot in battle.
A Horde cleric whose duties include shielding friendly forces.
Fizzcrank Bomber Flyby 01 is a mechanical bomber.
A Kor'kron war rider associated with the Horde's military.
A Fizzcrank fighter who angrily threatens to blast gnomish rivals and objects when told to return.
A Tuskarr tribesman, identified as a humanoid member of the Tuskarr community.
A female trapper who has been transformed, identified by that role rather than by a personal name.
Ursula Direbrew is a Dark Iron Brewmaiden associated with the Direbrew sisters encounter.
A Drakkari raptor mount, identified by its Drakkari association and its use as a mount.
A worgen in a frenzied state, defined by its agitation and loss of control.
A warhorse startled into alarm, marked by a sudden frightened state rather than an individual identity.
A shoveltusk scavenger of Dragonblight.
A frost wyrm.
A Wind Rider Master assigned to Vanguard Landing, offering fast travel.
Kareg is a named Wind Rider Master who offers air travel. His known line is “Guards!”; when aggroed, he summons an enraged wyvern.
A Conquest Hold outrider, identified by a place and role rather than a personal name.
Tecahuna is a beast.
An ancient Drakkari king, this creature enters combat and casts Drakkari Curse.
A giant identified as weakened.
Cartographer Tobias is a humanoid cartographer.
An elite humanoid known by the title Mistress of the Coldwind.
A humanoid identified as a Coldwind witch.
Grauf is a named creature in Skadi the Ruthless’s encounter. Grauf takes a deep breath, while Skadi comes within range of the harpoon launchers during the assault.

Snowfall Elk are beasts named as targets in Soar Hawkfury’s request to vaccinate them with Sintar’s vaccine. The quest describes the vial as releasing inoculating gas and asks for the elk to be vaccinated; it does not establish any individual elk’s outcome.
A mechanical clockwork gnome identified for Northrend.
A red riding drake, a beast.

The Essence of Warlord Jin'arrak is a summoned presence connected to the rites at Drakil'jin Ruins. During Kraz's task to reach Gan'jo in the spirit world, it objects, “How dare you summon me without an offering!”

Overseer Durval is one of four overseers Gavrock identifies with the runes of compulsion along Eastwind Shore, where Iron dwarves bind stone giants to fight. The overseers appear when the rune-weavers at their runes are defeated. When summoned, he threatens his opponent and defends the sons of iron.

Overseer Korgan is one of four overseers Gavrock identifies with the runes of compulsion along Eastwind Shore, where Iron dwarves bind stone giants to fight. The overseers appear when the rune-weavers at their runes are defeated. When summoned, he threatens his opponent and invokes the sons of iron, like the other overseers.

Overseer Lochli is one of four overseers Gavrock identifies with the runes of compulsion along Eastwind Shore, where Iron dwarves bind stone giants to fight. The overseers appear when the rune-weavers at their runes are defeated. When summoned, he threatens his opponent and invokes the sons of iron, like the other overseers.

Overseer Brunon is a rune-weaver of the sons of iron, stationed at a Rune of Compulsion used to bind stone giants and send them to fight in the north. Gavrock’s account names Brunon among the four overseers to defeat to disable the runes. When summoned, Brunon threatens attackers and challenges those who defy the sons of iron.
Grand Magus Telestra is a hostile magical combatant. In combat, she casts Fire Blast.
Grand Magus Telestra is a hostile magical combatant. In combat, she uses Time Stop and a spell named Critter.
Grand Magus Telestra is a hostile magical combatant. She casts Blizzard and Fire Blast.
Bloodbane's Mount, a beast.
Vix Chromeblaster is a self-help bookseller; shoppers can browse his goods.
A Frostbrood Slayer is an undead creature.
Grom'thar the Thunderbringer is a combative magnataur foe who threatens to devour challengers and reacts with surprise when one proves stronger than a magnataur. He attacks with a charge and thunder.
Builder Bezzle, a humanoid.
Builder Bozzle, a humanoid.

A depleted war golem used in Raegar Breakbrow’s power-cell task. It can absorb energy from dying lightning sentries and report when collection begins and finishes; the task describes the charged golem as fit to run only briefly and poor in combat.
A Dreadlord demon form labeled for warlock Metamorphosis.
The charged form of a war golem, a mechanical creature.
A plague zombie, an undead creature.
Xink’s summoned shredder announces that it is ready for woodland destruction. Its security features can also activate and send it back to base.
A mechanical Horde siege tank.
A Horde siege tank.
A Warsong shaman left injured amid the fighting. The shaman can still answer an attack with Earth Shock.
An injured Warsong soldier caught on the Plains of Nasam can be rescued from a Horde siege tank.
A wounded Warsong engineer can be pulled from the battlefield. Grateful for the rescue, the engineer plans to get the tank moving faster, bringing practical mechanical skill to the Horde assault.

Icefist Forager is a frightened creature that cries, “Run away!” and “I don't wanna die!” When summoned, it also calls out that the “big guy” will save them, showing it expects help from someone nearby.
A Dragonblight hippogryph taxi, a beast.
A Dalaran commoner.
This creature is the Headless Horseman's mount.
The Headless Horseman's mount is an undead creature.
A 7th Legion siege engineer works on a plague wagon and calls for cover while doing so. They joke that their work will make it look goblin-built.
The Brewmaiden responds to a particular emote by tossing Brewfest brew.
A 7th Legion test unit.
The Black Brewmaiden is a humanoid.
A warmage associated with Amber Ledge.
A Chilltusk forager who fears dying, urges others to run away, and hopes an unnamed big protector will save them.
A warmage associated with the Transitus Shield.
A bat used as transport in Howling Fjord.
A tiny blue dragon kept as a noncombat companion.
A tiny gold dragon kept as a noncombat companion.

Warlord Jin'arrak is a corrupted warlord tied to the Drakil'jin offering ritual. He welcomes a worthy offering, reacts in confusion to what is happening to him, and objects to being summoned without an offering. His defeat is meant to release tormented souls.
A mounted knight of the Onslaught, this combatant leaves his vehicle when killed.
A Scarlet commander.

The Image of Loken delivers orders to Iron Rune overseers through a communication at Dun Argol. Loken demands more war golems before the stone giant leader and his army reach Ulduar. He orders rune-smiths to convert compliant stone giants and destroy those who refuse, forbids mortal aid to the giants, and holds the overseer and thane responsible if the giants interfere with his work.
A beast called a Jormungar Worm.
Clayton Dubin J, known as Assured Quality, is a humanoid.

Foreman Kaleiki oversees the lumbermill at New Hearthglen, whose operations trouble Apothecary Vicky Levine's side. Vicky plans to draw him out by damaging the millwork; Kaleiki's response is an angry threat to the intruder.
A humanoid test dummy for rogues.
An undead forgotten gryphon.
A guardian spirit.
An emerald wisp.
A small Scourge plague spreader.
A gryphon associated with Wintergarde.
An emerald seedling.
A risen gryphon rider: a rider identified with a gryphon and described as risen.
A rat identified by the name “Let Them Not Rise!” Rat.
A ritual channeler, identified by its role.
A buried prisoner.
King Bjorn Visual is a visual representation of King Bjorn.
Argent Healer is a humanoid named for the Argent organization and a healer role.
King Haldor Visual is a visual representation of King Haldor.
King Ranulf Visual is a visual representation of King Ranulf.
King Tor Visual is a visual representation of King Tor.
Ice Giant, Northrend is a giant of Northrend.
Outhouse Stalker.
The Outhouse Invisible Man.
A spirit fount.
A helpless peasant of Wintergarde, this villager is one of the settlement’s ordinary people caught up in the region’s dangers.
A small termite associated with the Levine family, this creature is identified as part of their termite population.

The Spirit of Ursoc thanks those who aided him and praises the ancient druids for tearing down Vordrassil. He says its roots reached the dwelling of an ancient evil and warns of Yogg-Saron, the old god he calls the beast with a thousand maws, whose evil extends beyond those roots.
An unholy demonic archon.

Thel’zan the Duskbringer is an undead servant who reveres Arthas as his lord. He despises the frailty of his former mortal life and says the Lich King promised to erase that weakness. He boasts that his service helped Naxxramas return to Northrend, regards himself as saved and blessed, and offers the same salvation to others while commanding minions to rise.
Thel'zan is known as the Duskbringer.
An undead spirit of vengeance.
A Valiance Keep footman spectator.

Dalronn the Controller is a named, commanding fighter who rebukes Skarvald for rushing into battle without assessing the situation. When Skarvald falls, Dalronn calls him incompetent and orders him to return and be useful. Their exchange shows an abrasive partnership: Dalronn expects Skarvald at his side and treats him as a tool, while his own dying words reach toward glory.

Skarvald the Constructor is a named fighter who challenges Dalronn to join his attack. When Dalronn falls, Skarvald mocks him as a worthless necromancer who should not let death stop him; his own last words accept a warrior's death. Their exchange shows a combative partnership marked by mutual expectation and sharp contempt.
An Avenging Spirit Summoner.
Typhoon is an elemental.
An Onslaught Footman, a rank-and-file member of the Onslaught. This one appears in a summoned encounter and asks the sergeant what is happening, suggesting confusion about the immediate situation.

An Onslaught Footman in a summoned encounter. This one reacts to uncertainty by urging that both targets be killed as a precaution, giving him a markedly more alarmed and ruthless response than the footman who asks the sergeant what is happening.
Ducal's horse is a mount used in a passenger ride sequence.
A freed Alliance scout caught in a frightening encounter with nonhuman trappers. He urgently checks whether his companion was bitten, then warns that the trappers are not human and urges an escape.
A Silverbrook worgen summoned into an encounter and immediately set to attack.
A destructive ward that gathers power until fully charged.
Quarterflash’s mechanical homing bot.
The Winterfin First Responder is a humanoid.

High Abbot Landgren is a defiant figure who recognizes the player's disguise and says the Master sees all. He invites the player to follow him to a private place, then says he knows the player has harmed his compatriots and refuses to die by the player's hand. He declares he will choose his own manner of leaving the world and hopes to return if the grand admiral's will permits it.

npcs.name: Scarlet Raven Priest Image - Female Transform

records.text: A female Scarlet Raven Priest image used for a transformation.

npcs.name: Scarlet Raven Priest Image - Male Transform

records.text: A male Scarlet Raven Priest image used for a transformation.

This portrayal of Prince Arthas pursues revenge against Mal’Ganis. Furious that Uther has recalled his troops, he orders the ships burned to prevent their departure and dismisses Muradin’s objections. He calls Frostmourne their salvation, offers to bear any curse to save his homeland, and declares that he will pay any price to save his people.
A Westfall Brigade hunter spots a skunk, rabbit, and fawn travelling together and remarks on the odd sight. He then says he’ll be dining on venison, giving this hunter a blunt, predatory outlook.
A Forgotten Soul is an undead spirit associated with the Forgotten Shore. It casts 'Permanent Feign Death'.
An Amberpine Hunter is a hunter associated with Amberpine.

Captain Luc Valonforth speaks as a military commander addressing his men and an emissary. He says the prince is away and that Lord Uther requested the troops be recalled; in another line, he urges his men to cut through the woods against the undead. His words place him in a force caught up in the prince’s absence and the campaign against the undead.
Caden Barleybrew is identified with the Brew of the Month Club.

Muradin stands alongside Arthas during the pursuit of Frostmourne. He recognizes the inscription as a warning that the blade is cursed, urges Arthas to abandon it and return home, and challenges Arthas over his pursuit of vengeance and betrayal of his men. He later becomes confused about his own identity.
Vengeful Bambina is a critter.
A Brew of the Month Club brew vendor.
Lohger is identified with the Brew of the Month Club.
An Alliance emissary whose reported news concerns undead-held roads and the expedition's recall to Lordaeron. He relays a royal edict and says Lord Uther persuaded the king to recall the expedition.
A Northrend gryphon rider.
A gryphon raised into an undead-aligned state.
A blue dragon vision associated with Unu'pe.
A humanoid Tuskarr vision.
A humanoid Vrykul vision.
A humanoid Gorloc vision.
A small rat and critter.
Grizzlesnout is a named beast that casts Gnaw Bone in combat.
A white-armored gryphon.
A Frigid Ghoul is an undead creature whose combat behavior includes casting Rot Armor. It is defined here by that battle role, rather than by an individual name or a service.
A Swift Zhevra is a beast identified by its quick-moving kind. Its name describes an animal type, without establishing a personal identity or a distinct story role.
Penguin, Northrend names a Northrend penguin, a beast rather than a personally named individual. The name identifies its animal kind and region.
A Mindless Ghoul is an undead creature whose name marks it as mindless. It is identified by that creature kind and trait, rather than by an individual name or service.
A Kor'kron Windrager is a humanoid identified by the Kor'kron name.

Darna Honeybock is a Brewfest Agent who warns that Coren Direbrew and the Dark Iron dwarves threaten Brewfest. Her warning points the listener toward the Brewfest spy in the Grim Guzzler, who can provide more about the plot.
Rizzy Fizzstout is identified as a Brewfest Agent, one of the named personnel associated with the festival.

A 7th Legion soldier serving with the Alliance in Dragonblight, this elite talks casually with fellow troops and addresses a tank driver as part of the crew. He boasts that his uncle McGoyver in Valgarde is a “Pro,” laughs off a tale about sand gnomes, and asks whether the driver rescued villagers.

A hulking undead corpse, this hostile creature lurches through its surroundings. Its records show it can move while retaining the blunt, imposing form its name describes; no further personal identity or allegiance is established.
A fetid troll corpse, an undead creature.
A risen undead shadowcaster that casts Shadow Bolt in combat.
A Jintha'kalar necromancer, an undead creature.
An undead image of the Lich King.
Tatjana is a Wolfcult initiate. Sasha describes Tatjana as Anatoly’s wife and a former horse-handler, and wants her brought back alive to the White Pine Trading Post as leverage to make Anatoly talk.
Tatjana is identified as a Wolfcult Initiate and is unconscious.
This is a wolf-spirit visual.
A vengeful nether drake.
A phantasmal mammoth that uses Charge in combat.
A Temple Caller.
A phantasmal wolf that uses Furious Howl in combat.
A phantasmal cloudscraper, a beast. It casts Chain Lightning in combat.
A phantasmal ogre, a humanoid. It casts Bloodlust when its health falls between zero and 30 percent.
A phantasmal naga, a humanoid creature. It casts Water Tomb in combat.
A phantasmal murloc, a humanoid creature. It uses poison in combat.
A phantasmal air elemental. It casts Lightning Shield when combat begins.
A phantasmal fire elemental. It casts Blaze in combat.
Phantasmal Water is a hostile water elemental that attacks with a volley of water bolts.
A Wintergarde gryphon rider of the 7th Legion, serving as an armed member of that force.
Crashin' Thrashin' Racer is a mechanical racer.
Ontok Shatterhorn is an arena vendor who offers goods to browse.

Dahlia Suntouch served as keeper of a shrine blessed by Alexstrasza and offered herself to the Life-Binder in life. She says the Lich King’s forces reached sacred dragonflight lands, and that she fell to the death knight Bloodbane. After being freed from undeath, she thanks her liberator and says a new keeper must take her place; her words reflect her own experience and knowledge.
A swift zhevra, a fast-moving wild equine creature.
A Scourge ghoul attacking the shrine’s canyons during the defense led by Captain Iskandar.
A dragon known as a Wyrmrest Defender.

An emerald drake who welcomes a friend and urges them to hold on. It can use Dream Funnel to heal other drakes at the cost of its own health, warning that Leeching Poison helps offset the drain. It identifies Mage-Lord Urom as the next target and warns he may not be alone.
An undead Player Skeleton.
The Prophet Tharon'ja is a level-76 undead elite.
A mechanical creature identified as a Crashin' Thrashin' Racer Driver.
A beast identified as a Brewfest Riding Kodo.
A Great Brewfest Kodo.
A Drakkari invader, this hostile combatant moves toward a position.
Ironhide is the bear offered as an early opponent in the Conquest Pit’s wrestling fights.
Torgg Thundertotem is presented as an unusually large, crazed Northrend furbolg and a Conquest Pit fight opponent.
Rustblood is a named mechanical fighter linked to an encounter involving Grennix. It attacks with head smashes, cleaves, knockbacks and lightning bolts.
Horgrenn Hellcleave is a named contender in the Conquest Pit. The challenge directs opponents to defeat him and then speak with Bookie Vel'jen for a reward.
A Drakkari bat mount associated with Drakkari invaders.

Conqueror Krenna is a named authority who rebukes someone for acting behind her back and disregarding her orders. Her scripted threats, including a reference to worgs avoiding a corpse, present her as severe and intimidating.
A master necromancer, presented as a powerful combatant.
A ghoul minion: an undead subordinate combatant.
A creature named Frostsabre Vehicle.
A creature named Wild Elekk Vehicle Version.
A creature named Currency Token Test Wizard.
The Infinite Adversary is a powerful hostile creature. It casts spells in combat.
The Infinite Hunter is a powerful hostile creature. It casts a spell when hit by a spell.

The Infinite Agent is a powerful hostile creature. Archmage Timear identifies Infinite agents as a threat to the timeline and names them as targets in the Culling of Stratholme. It casts a spell in combat.
A Drakkari invader, one of the Drakkari forces represented in the world.
A Drakkari invader, one of the Drakkari forces represented in the world.

An amber drake who welcomes riders and coaches them in combat from the air. Amber explains how Temporal Rift helps enemies take extra damage and generate Shock Charges for Shock Lance, then points toward Mage-Lord Urom on the Band of Transmutation and warns that the conjurer may have company.

A ruby drake who welcomes riders and coaches them in combat from the air. Ruby explains Martyr's protective use for other drakes and cautions that it leaves the Ruby vulnerable, advising Evasive Maneuvers. Ruby also points toward Mage-Lord Urom on the Band of Transmutation and warns that the conjurer may have company.
A gryphon designated for Wintergarde taxi duty.
An undead image of Sapphiron.
An undead image of Gothik.
An undead image of Thane Korth'azz.
An undead image of Lady Blaumeux.
An undead image of Sir Zeliek.
An undead image of Grobbulus.
An undead image of Thaddius.
An undead image of Faerlina.
An undead image of Maexxna.
An undead image of Heigan.
An undead image of Loatheb.
An undead image of Gluth.

An injured 7th Legion soldier hides from the Scourge near the chain guns and barricades east and west of Wintergarde Mausoleum. A chain gunner can call a soldier from hiding and cover the rescue with fire; the soldier's recorded responses express relief and thanks.
Reincarnated Skytalon is a critter.

Lord Itharius identifies Weakened Overseer Deathgaze as a powerful Scourge foe at Jintha'kalar, far to the northeast. Deathgaze is one of three targets for a seed that will weaken them enough for the adventurer to face alone.

Lord Itharius identifies Weakened Turgid the Vile as a powerful Scourge foe in the ruined barracks at the Carrion Fields. Turgid is one of three targets for a seed that will weaken them enough for the adventurer to face alone.

This weakened reanimated frost wyrm is one of the wyrms circling north near Galakrond's Rest. Lord Itharius names one such wyrm among three powerful Scourge foes that a seed will weaken enough for the adventurer to face alone.

A Scourge target inside the Wintergarde Mausoleum, associated with the forces gathered below its crypts. Yord Icebeard includes it among the Naxxramas Scourge that must be dealt with before the assault can reach the inner chamber.
An Ebon Gargoyle is an undead creature called forth by a death knight to fight at their side. Its presence is tied to the death knight's summoning.
Glengarry Adams is identified with the 7th Legion.
A Shadowfiend Guardian is a demonic guardian creature.
The Wintergrasp Fighter Plane is an aerial combat craft identified with the Wintergrasp conflict.
A Wintergarde gryphon used as a mount.
A plagued roach, an animal.
A Shadow Void, an elemental.
A plagued resident, a humanoid.
Patchy is a named gas-cloud creature.
A mechanical bomber associated by name with Wintergrasp.
A critter identified as a Plagued Vermin.

Highlord Bolvar Fordragon invokes honor, courage, compassion and justice when addressing Thel’zan, recalling the cleric’s former service to the Argent Dawn against the Scourge. He asks how Father Inigo Montoy became what he once hated. In his victory address, Bolvar celebrates the Alliance’s success at Wintergarde, expects the 7th Legion to clear the remaining Scourge, and directs the victorious fighter to Angrathar.
A beast designated Fanggore Worg Disguise.
Plagued Pet is a non-combat pet.
A generic woodland squirrel that can follow another creature.
An undead minion of Thel’zan.
A Wintergrasp siege catapult, a vehicle that can be boarded through its spell-click interaction.
A Wintergrasp shredder, a mechanical combat unit.
A Valgarde gryphon used to carry passengers.

A Valgarde gryphon rider who carries people by air. The rider directs a passenger toward Icehammer inside a vrykul building and urges them to fight, then announces departure. This supports a brisk, encouraging manner in the moment.
Malcolm Moore has a dog named Scruffy. In a scripted scene, he remarks that a storm is coming, asks what Scruffy found, then tells him to guard the house while he goes to find a soldier.
Scruffy is Malcolm Moore's dog. Malcolm addresses him as “pal” and “boy” and tells him to guard the house; Scruffy growls and follows a path.
Fire Revenant, Northrend, is an elemental.
Infinite Assailant is dragonkin.
An Infinite Destroyer is a dragonkin creature.
An Infinite Chrono-Magus with a hostile encounter role.

A future version of the player who appears to help defend an hourglass. He warns that attackers are coming and urges the player to keep them away; he says he cannot reveal the player’s future because Chromie forbade it. He is unsettled by the time-travel paradox and insists that both versions have a stake in what happens.
An elite Infinite Timerender that uses Time Lapse in combat.
A pink elekk identified as a riding mount.
A Wintergrasp bomber cockpit: a vehicle component rather than an individual person or animal.
An angry jungle gnome who appears as a summoned figure.
An ethereal soul-trader who captures essence and trades with its summoner, offering a share of what it gathers.
A trainer for death knights.
An Alliance recruiter, a humanoid.
A Horde recruiter, a humanoid.
The Horde's herald is a humanoid whose title marks it as the Horde's representative.
The Alliance's herald is a humanoid whose title marks it as the Alliance's representative.
Lou is a named cabin boy who ferries passengers to Scalawag Point. He greets the trip with exuberant pirate cries, then sets off along his route.
Harry's Bomber begins its route when a passenger rides it.
A Pumpkin Soldier is an elemental creature.
Orf is identified as a helmsman, a vessel's steering crew member.
The Helmsman's Ship is the vessel associated with its helmsman.

A Horde commander who leads from the front, this combatant charges into battle, rallies nearby allies with Battle Shout, and fights with Whirlwind. When engaged, the commander can also break free of Frozen Prison.
A pink elekk in a parade.
Your Inner Turmoil is a quest-target entity tied to the Frostblade Shrine meditation in The Cleansing.
An eroded shardling, classified as a giant.
A forged iron trogg.
An earthen dwarf, this combatant has a formidable build and serves as a martial presence among the earthen.
A malformed ooze associated with Sjonnir, it is a dungeon creature with an aggressive combat role.
A forged iron dwarf associated with Sjonnir, this sturdy combatant is part of the dungeon's hostile forces.
A Dark Rune Protector, this armored defender meets threats with a charge, closing distance to engage intruders.
A Dark Rune Stormcaller, this combatant attacks with Shadow Word: Pain in both normal and heroic dungeon encounters.
An iron golem assigned a custodian's role, this mechanical combatant uses a crushing attack to hinder its opponent's armor.
D.I.S.C.O.
Lieutenant Icehammer holds the rank of lieutenant.

A Wyrmrest dragon who speaks with reverence for the ancestors whose bones lie across Dragonblight and their spirits in the Chamber of the Aspects. He welcomes the freedom of flying beyond Wyrmrest Temple and condemns the Scourge’s destruction, calling for its aberrations to be stopped.
An elemental called Ethereal Mutagen - Pet.
Ethereal Mutagen - Player.

Grand Necrolord Antiok directs Scourge forces at Galakrond's Rest, demanding more frost wyrms for Angrathar and urging his troops to keep attacking. He guards the ancient grave and wields the Scythe of Antiok to control wyrms. He threatens intruders and declares that Galakrond's bones will rise again.
Antiok's Mount is an undead mount.
A bloodworm is a small critter.
An elite dragonkin designated Wyrmrest Vanquisher (Bones).
An undead creature identified as a Rotting Abomination, with rot as its defining trait.
An Argent Shieldman who uses Rend and Shield Block in combat.
A hostile Conquest Hold windrager who rallies for the Horde and calls for Alliance enemies to be killed.

A 7th Legion gryphon rider who transports an ally toward Amberpine Lodge and scouts Conquest Hold for Horde wind riders. The rider is confident about evading them and speaks with open contempt for the Horde.
A Wintergrasp siege vehicle, the Demolisher is an interactive piece of battlefield machinery.
Lemming is a critter.
An enraged skeleton, this undead creature is a hostile combatant.
Warlord Tartek took the Mistwhisper Treasure to a camp. He claims it as his own and taunts anyone who tries to take it back, threatening them with a dragon.

Soo-holu is a protector the Great Ones left at the shrines. Called to the Lightning Shrine with a tainted crystal, he binds with a summoner's body and lends his power against nearby Frenzyheart wolvar.
Kartak the Abominable is a being whose bond with a host's body stirs rage within the host.

Watery Lord is an elemental lord associated with the fluid sought by Hexxer Ubungo at The Argent Stand. Ubungo plans to combine links from elementals into a tether to summon one of their lords, amid elemental incursions near the Drak'Sotra Fields.

Jaloot is an Oracle who speaks for his people in an exuberant, simple manner. He delights in shiny treasures, especially his crystal, and is protective of Oracle treasures. He admires the Mistcaller’s skill at controlling weather with shrine crystals and believes the Great Ones protect the Oracles because they are good. He faces visitors and their dragon companion with playful defiance, and warmly offers friendship and help.
Ugly Pete is a humanoid.

Crusader Jonathan is a wounded crusader left behind in the fighting around Drak’Sotra, where the Scourge drove back his forces. He is bleeding and fears he is near death; when aided, he thanks his rescuer and says he would otherwise have died.
Crusader Lamoof is one of the wounded crusaders Dr. Rogers seeks after Drak'Sotra falls to the Scourge. He is losing blood and fears this is the end, though he asks whether they can move out.
A beast known as Mindless Aberration (Unkillable).
Crusader Josephine is one of the wounded crusaders Dr. Rogers seeks after Drak'Sotra falls to the Scourge. She says she cannot go on and expresses gratitude to the friend who saved her life.

Hexxer Ubungo describes the Muddled Prophet of Sseratus as arrogant at the altar and a potential threat to the Argent Crusade. He proposes altered mojo to weaken and confuse the prophet, while acknowledging that its effects are only a theory.
Snowflake uses Frostbolt in normal and heroic dungeon combat.
Scourgeheart Drakkari is an elite undead Drakkari.
Guerrero is a beast whose combat behavior includes Threatening Growl and Rend.
Don Carlos, Young, Hatless is a humanoid, distinguished by the identifying epithet “Young, Hatless.”
Iron Sludge is a creature.
The Unstable Sphere is a creature associated with the Oculus.
Guerrero is an elite beast.
Don Carlos is an elite humanoid.
Grief Void.
A goblin construction crew.
Dusk is involved in the search for the phylactery. During that encounter, Dusk motions toward the icy water below.
A retired Onslaught warhorse.

Prince Valanar is a San'layn who reports to a superior about cultists infiltrating Alliance power structures and his growing influence over human minds. He describes villagers in his forces as wary of their exotic allies and offers to deal brutally with intruders.
Archmage Pentarus' flying machine warns of missile lock and announces evasive maneuvers. Along its flight, it casts a cosmetic flame dart.
A mechanical rocket launcher.
An elite undead tomb stalker.
An elite necromancer who uses spells in combat.
A gorged lurking basilisk with an unusual crystal-making role: when struck by the spell associated with Gluttonous Lurkers, it casts Create Basilisk Crystals.

Dajik is a Frenzyheart hunter and teacher who has trained many of his people and even tries teaching outsiders. He speaks casually about taking the big-tongues' homes, dismissing them as ugly. Yet he would rather eat bristlepine than chase chickens; losing to one seems embarrassing, though he admits they move fast.
An elemental known as The Etymidian.
Griz Gutshank is an arena vendor who offers goods for browsing.
Snaggletooth is a humanoid.
Slobbermouth is a humanoid.

A Venture Co. pilot on air patrol, this company representative warns intruders that no one interferes with the Venture Company. Its greeting presents the pilot as defending the company against trespassers.
Nozronn's Eye.
An undead Sanguine Spirit.
The Tribunal of the Ages.
Azure Ring Captain is an elite associated by name with the Azure Ring.
Dark Matter Target is a mechanical encounter target.
Arcane Beam is a mechanical entity identified by its beam name.
Venture Co. Air Patrol is a flying creature identified as an air patrol.

Nozronn speaks through his bones when Soo-rahm’s incense is used. He agrees to aid the oracle’s visitor by describing where Farunn can be found, then instructs the visitor to claim the prize and leave the land in peace, since they do not belong there.
Searing Gaze.
A coyote spirit classified as a noncombat pet.
A powerful ley-whelp that uses Arcane Bolt in both its normal and heroic forms.
A ravenous plaguehound, a beast associated with the Scourge.
A Sholazar Witch Light is a summoned magical presence.
An Acherus Deathcharger, a beast.
A captive crocolisk.
A Wintergrasp siege engine, a mechanical vehicle.
Bushwhacker is a named crocolisk described locally as the basin’s largest and known for ambushing prey. His ambush is in River’s Heart; he sniffs the air at an unusual scent.

Grand Apothecary Putress leads research into a zombie-plague cure at Shattrath’s Terrace of Light, presented as aid to the Horde and Alliance against the Lich King. He says the ends justify the means and frames the research as a way for the Forsaken to earn respect. Short of volunteers, he welcomes recruits’ fresh blood for experiments.
An escaped gladiator and humanoid combatant.
A ravenous crocolisk whose presence is marked by a low guttural growl. It attacks and, on death, casts Summon Shaman Vekjik.

Shaman Vekjik is a Frenzyheart shaman who reacts angrily when someone helps Rainspeaker, calling that person a traitor and threatening to tell the village. He says the Frenzyheart will no longer trust them, then scurries toward Frenzyheart Hill.
Slurpo Fizzykeg is identified as a Brewfest Agent.
The Stratholme Citizen is a hostile Stratholme figure who casts Void Strike when a target comes within five yards.
The Stratholme Resident is a hostile Stratholme figure who casts Arcane Wave in combat.
The Trapdoor Ambusher is a creature identified by its trapdoor ambush role.
Meeda is identified as a banker.
A Drakkari spirit associated with the Drakkari.
A risen Vrykul berserker: an undead Vrykul identified by its forceful martial role.
A risen Vrykul magus, combining an undead Vrykul identity with a spellcaster’s role.
A red-variant blightspreader bearing the Forsaken label.
A scientist identified with the Forsaken label and a blight backpack.
Riding Fizzcrank Flyer Taxi is a taxi.
Riding Dragonhawk (A) is identified as a riding dragonhawk.
Big Battle Bear is identified as a bear.
Slim's Test Mage is identified as a mage.
Slim's Test Warlock is identified as a warlock.
A Burning Skimmer that casts Immolation.
A humanoid 7th Legion siege engineer, identified by military role rather than a personal name.
A sparkling hare that scampers about at random when summoned.
A lesser air elemental that casts Lightning Bolt once combat begins.
An undead human male known by the abbreviated designation “DK,” rather than a personal name.
He is known as Zeptek the Destroyer.
A Northrend Leatherworking Trainer.
An Acherus Ghoul.
A Drakkari captive.

A captive footman trapped in a nerubian cocoon. After being freed, he can express relief, say he thought he was done for, and thank the person who helped him. The cocooned soldiers are Captain Rupert’s own.
A human female Death Knight.
DK is a female dwarf undead.
DK is a female gnome undead.
DK (Night Elf Female) is an undead.
DK (Draenei Female) is an undead.
DK (Dwarf Male) is an undead.
DK (Gnome Male) is an undead.
DK (Night Elf Male) is an undead.
DK (Draenei Male) is an undead.
A male Blood Elf death knight, classified as undead.
A male Orc death knight, classified as undead.
A male Forsaken death knight, classified as undead.
A male Troll death knight, classified as undead.
A male Tauren death knight, classified as undead.
A female blood elf death knight, classified as undead.
A female troll death knight, classified as undead.
A female orc death knight, classified as undead.
A female Forsaken death knight.
An undead female tauren designated DK.
Unbound Charger is an undead creature.

Hemet Nesingwary tells animated battle stories: he rode into a fight on Stampy, recalls a fearsome beast and a shaking battlefield, and credits an adventurer’s skill and teamwork alongside his own. He addresses Dorian and calls their trophy a memento of victory.
Stampy is a beast associated with the events of Post-partum Aggression.
A young nether ray kept as a noncombat companion.
Material You is a summoned figure associated with the Altar of Quetz'lun. When summoned, it says, “You leave your material body behind!” and is linked to the altar's Material You's Mirror Image Aura.
Runebladed Axe.

This portrayal of the Lich King credits Drakuru’s betrayal of the Drakkari Empire with providing a new army. He orders Drakuru to cleanse Zul’Drak, promising greater power for success and ruin for failure. In another address, he calls a betrayal amusing, declares that he is sparing the unnamed betrayer for showing potential, and warns that their next meeting will require more to justify that person’s life.
Sindragosa is the undead Queen of the Frostbrood.
Ronakada is titled a blademaster.
The Eye of Acherus is a controllable summoned eye that launches toward a destination.
Quartermaster Ozorg is a named humanoid quartermaster.
A vampiric batling is a small bat creature.

Nalorakk is a named, powerful figure who warns that the Drakkari and their gods are headed toward mutual ruin. His words show concern for the consequences of their conflict, rather than simple triumph over it.
Jan'alai urges that “the spotted one” be sought, saying their fates are entwined.
Akil'zon is a named beast who says that a woman is chained and that a way must be found to free her.
Halazzi is a named beast who directs a mortal toward an altar and warns that what must be done there may be difficult or impossible.

Nass is a blight-scarred helper whom Stefan uses to collect hair samples from scourged trolls. Stefan says Nass is deaf, blind, mostly numb, and virtually immune to blight; Nass’s own remarks complain about the trip to Zul’Drak, the work, and lost dignity.
A worn bloodworm.

Released Offspring of Har'koa are her children, whom the Drakkari transformed into monstrosities. Har'koa asks that they be slain and released from their nightmare with one of her whiskers, restoring them to life.
A vengeful ghoul, an undead creature.
A frost wyrm mount.
A Scarlet Commander's riding horse.
A Val'kyr battle-maiden who tells a fallen champion it is not yet their time and urges them to rise and fight again.
Known as Wants Orange, this creature reacts to the Toss Orange spell.
Wants Papaya reacts when hit by Toss Papaya.
Steaming Valve is a mechanism that casts Cosmetic Steam Blast.
A creature known as Wants Fire.
Distillo-matic 5000 is a mechanical creature.
Water Spout.
A humanoid construction worker, identified by its laboring role.
An undead Scourge disguise.

Foreman Wick is overseeing the effort to return a statue to its place at Stormwind Harbor. He says the crew lacks discipline and blames a dwarf coworker for undermining him. He wants the statue moved up the ramp and back as quickly as possible.

Mason Goldgild is a member of the Royal Stonecutter's Guild, working with Wick to move a statue out of the water. He favored using a crane and timed explosives; he now worries that Wick's ramp plan has left the statue angled wrong and that the work will take a long time.
An underwater construction worker, carrying out building work beneath the water. The role is practical and centered on construction at an underwater site.
Corpse Explosion Rubble.
A construction worker presented with dwarf appearance.
A quest-credit target associated with The Lifewarden's Wrath, which directs the player to use Freya's Horn atop the Glimmering Pillar to channel her power through the crystal.
A dwarf working in construction.
An adventurous dwarf hunting fruit who recognizes another fruit seeker and asks for an orange, bananas, or a papaya. A tug draws an irritated protest, and help is met with thanks.
An elite knight of the Silver Hand.
A wolf rider associated with Orgrimmar.
A Scarlet gryphon rider.
A riding horse identified as a charger.
Grayson Ironwing is a flight master. His greeting asks where a traveler would like to fly.
A riding gyrocopter used for taxi transport.
A blood maggot is vermin.
A spirit wolf is a beast.

Heb'Jin is identified as the leader of the Heb'Drakkar, and Dagoda describes him rallying his forces from the bat rookery. When challenged at his drum, Heb'Jin answers with threats, including, “Now you gonna die!”
Apothecary Deathguard is an apothecary identified with the Deathguard.
Apothecary Researcher is identified as an apothecary engaged in research.
Heb'Jin's Bat is the bat associated with Heb'Jin's bat-rookery encounter. Dagoda says a net can trap the bat when it lands, separating it from Heb'Jin during the fight.
Vic’s self-replicating abomination.

Pilot Vic warns companions about vines, rough winds and incoming attackers, urging them to use their rockets quickly. He reports heavy Scourge damage, a glacier advancing from Icecrown and undead everywhere, and is eager for an unnamed professor to learn what they have seen.
An undead messenger known as the Abominable Messenger.
A humanoid known as the Mysterious Gypsy.
A Dark Rider of Acherus whose warning invokes the realm of shadows.
Seat Squatter - LAB is a named figure.

Har'koa's Kitten speaks as a grateful, alert companion: it thanks the person who saved it and says it can return the favor. During a dangerous passage, it warns them to hold on, then reacts with dismay at Quetz'lun's death and urges stillness so they can sneak past the prophet.
A summoned flying creature that casts Scourge Disguise during its route, removes the disguise, and ejects passengers.
A Frostbrood Vanquisher is an undead creature.
Teller Halder is identified as a banker.
Teller Duta is identified as a banker.
Teller Banning is identified as a banker.
Brittle Golem is a golem whose defining trait is brittleness.
Scarlet Stablehand is a stablehand identified by the Scarlet name.
Molten Golem is a golem defined by its molten nature.
Vic's Flying Machine is a damaged aircraft: its engine has blown, and the instruction associated with it is to fly it back to Lakeside Landing.
An undead eagle, identified as a beast.
A basic loot piñata marked “Hit Me!”
A First Aid loot piñata marked “Hit Me!”
A Skittering Swarmer, classified as a beast.
An undead infector that casts Acid Splash when it dies.
A humanoid named Ol' Nelly.
A humanoid messenger identified with the Apothecary Society.
Slim's Unkillable Boss is a humanoid.
An Alarmed Blightguard is an undead guard described as alarmed; it moves about rather than remaining still.
This Dark Rider of Acherus is a combatant who casts Icy Touch, Blood Strike, and Plague Strike. It exits its vehicle when it dies.
A target associated with a Dark Rider, represented as a creature rather than a conversational character.
An explosive charge helper that announces a five-second countdown, then four and three seconds.
A battleground demolisher built as a vehicle-like creature.
An armored gryphon identified for neutral taxi use.

The Spirit of Quetz'lun speaks as a hostile spirit who taunts opponents with death and the afterlife. It says it has returned to invite them to an underworld housewarming and expects its prophet to remain with it eternally.
Salanar the Horseman addresses a death knight, praises their performance, and directs them to return to the world of the living for their reward.

The Drained Prophet of Quetz'lun is described as a prophet in a drained state. Har'koa links the prophet to a ritual at Quetz'lun's altar, intended to draw her spirit into the material world so she can reclaim her power from the prophet.
Known as the Hand of Drakuru.
A humanoid paladin known as the Reverent Paladin.
A reverent priest.
A Scarlet miner working in the Havenshire Mines. He wonders where a found object came from and wants to get it down to the ships before the foreman sees it; after that, he says he can rest.
A Scarlet Ghoul, an undead enemy created when Gothik's plague device is used on Scarlet miners. It snarls, “Die $N, die!”
A Scarlet Ghost that attacks when it respawns.
Siltslither Eel is an eel, an aquatic creature.
Dead Mam'toth Disciple Transform is a creature form representing a dead Mam'toth disciple, rather than an identified individual.
Blood of the Old God is a creature associated with Old God corruption. It casts Corruption of the Old God when something is within two yards.

Drostan treats the fighting as a contest, taunting the player about their kill counts and boasting of his own: he calls out numbers from nine to twenty-five and says they have a competition. He also boasts that his mother could hunt faster than the player.
The Scourge Gryphon is associated with flight: it casts Flight and can be called from a cannon when ready to return.

A Drakkari chieftain drawn into Drakuru's attack on the army north of Voltarus. Drakuru's scheme uses abominations to provoke the chieftains into appearing, then sends his pet Shalewing to seize them and carry them away. The chieftain is a target in that plan, not its author.
Shalewing is described by Drakuru as his pet and part of his plan against the Drakkari army. When chieftains appear, Shalewing is sent to snatch them and bring them to Drakuru.
A skeletal minion.
A guard whose title marks a reverent or devout character.
Frosty is a creature known by that name.
A Scarlet Gryphon Rider is a creature.
A Scarlet Ghoul is driven by hunger, muttering that it must feed and can smell nearby flesh. Its brief words focus on finding food.
A Havenshire mare, a female horse.
A Havenshire stallion, a male horse.
A Scourge gryphon.
A dark rider's fixed mount, a beast.
An Anub'ar Crusher that calls for forces to be redirected when the gate is breached and can enter a frenzy.
An Anub'ar champion.
An Anub'ar necromancer.
A spark of Ionar, an elemental creature.
An enchanted tiki dervish that changes its form.
Dansel Adams is an undead figure.
The Inscriber, a humanoid known as the Designer Extraordinaire.
Ionar Invis Stalker.

Malmortis is a Scourge-aligned servant of the master, stationed at Voltarus to show prospects the operation and its blight-crystal stores. He keeps the project secret from outsiders while preparing subjects with a special treatment that grants them greater powers. He recognizes the visitor as someone whose supply contribution has been substantial.

Scarlet Lord Jesseriah McCree is a Scarlet Crusader who resists questioning about the Crimson Dawn before revealing what little he knows. He says the Light speaks to the High General, who decides who may leave and who must stay, and mentions an expected courier from Hearthglen. He also says he once worked for Grand Inquisitor Isillien; his account offers no fuller explanation of the movement.
Haiphoon bears the epithet the Great Tempest and is an elemental.

The Prophet of Akali speaks as an agent of a master who wants Akali's blood and power. He declares the confrontation with Akali done, then threatens to come for Har'koa and tells her to carry the warning back to her masters. His words place him in an active conflict with Akali's side.
Haiphoon, the Great Tempest is an elemental.

High Inquisitor Valroth presents himself as a champion of the Crusade and the Light, threatening to purge the Scourge and claiming he has come to deliver those seeking deliverance. He addresses an opponent as Scourge and calls them a coward; he also uses Valroth's Smite and Renew.
A Frost Vrykul of Type A, classified as humanoid.
A Frost Vrykul of Type B, classified as humanoid.
A Frost Vrykul of Type C, classified as humanoid.
A Charged War Golem designated as a non-combat pet.
A Crimson Acolyte is a creature that casts Holy Fury while out of combat.
An Anti-Magic Barrier (Quest) totem.
Disgruntled Bug is a critter.
Spirit of Ha-Khalan is among the evil spirits Soo-nee asks to have cleansed from Sholazar’s waters. In combat it uses Thick Hide, Jagged Tooth Snap and Powerful Bite.
A dockhand with a bag.

Akil'zon is a named, powerful figure who speaks through a summoned vision. He warns Khufu and the adventurer that their future looks doomed and that the prophet may prove too powerful, while insisting they must still try.

Halazzi speaks to Khufu and the adventurer through a summoned vision, saying that he and the others have been called again and have wisdom to share. He warns of great peril and urges swift action to save them and Har'koa.

Jan'alai's message explains that gusty essences from Quetz'lun's deceased wardens are needed to draw Quetz'lun near, and that both rarities must be delivered to Har'koa. The words are delivered through a summoned vision.

Nalorakk's message calls for the guardian's unblemished heart as proof of defiance and strength, and names jealous Zim'Rhuk as the one keeping those who harbor it. He speaks through a summoned vision.

The Prophet of Akali is a Drakkari foe who claims Akali’s power and seeks to reach Zim'Torga. He recognizes the adventurer as the one who killed Akali, calls them a foreign invader, and threatens to kill them. Har'koa's appearance startles him.
Spirit of Atha is one of the evil spirits Soo-nee wants driven from Sholazar's waters during the Cleansing Song task. It attacks with Aqua Jet.
Spirit of Koosu is one of the evil spirits Soo-nee wants driven from Sholazar's waters during the Cleansing Song task. It attacks with Poison Bolt.
A mechanical chopper designated for the Horde.
It's A Chopper, Baby (Alliance) is a mechanical chopper.

Har’koa confronts Drakkari who are performing a ritual, demands that they release those they hold, and protects them from the Drakkari’s hands. After the rescue, she thanks her rescuers for saving everyone and says she will see them back at Zim’Torga.
An Anub'ar Crypt Fiend, an undead creature.
The Outhouse Invisible Woman.
An Anub'ar Champion is a combatant role among the Anub'ar. It uses Rend in combat, distinguishing its fighting role from the crypt fiends and necromancers.
An Anub'ar Crypt Fiend is a combatant role among the Anub'ar. It uses Infected Wound in combat, giving it a close-quarters threat distinct from the champion's Rend and the necromancer's Shadow Bolt.
An Anub'ar Necromancer is a combatant role among the Anub'ar. It casts Shadow Bolt out of combat, unlike the champion's Rend and the crypt fiend's Infected Wound.

The Scarlet Courier stops to investigate a strange-looking tree, then realizes it is not a tree and calls for guards. The brief exchange gives the courier a moment of alert discovery amid its delivery role.
A Bloodmoon Servant is a combatant whose fighting behavior includes becoming enraged when its health falls to a low level.
PattyMacks The Duece is a humanoid.

Bishop Lazaril is an Alliance bishop and quest giver at Shattrath's Terrace of Light. The effort against the Lich King's plague and invasion is framed as cooperation between Horde and Alliance. Its Light-infused artifact project draws on the naaru's Light and the faithful's benedictions to aid the Alliance's campaign toward Northrend.

Mini Tyrael is a named, small creature with simple but distinctive reactions: he can fall asleep or become enraged, responds to a received dance emote, and speaks when hit by a spell. These behaviors give him a playful, animated presence.
An Anub'ar Champion is a dungeon combatant identified by its champion role among the Anub'ar. This foe uses Rend in combat.
An Anub'ar Crypt Fiend is a dungeon combatant identified by its crypt fiend role. Its combat behavior includes Infected Wound.
An Anub'ar Necromancer is an undead spellcaster among the Anub'ar. In combat, it uses Shadow Bolt.
A Val'kyr Battle-maiden, an undead warrior.
A humanoid high commander named Galvar Pureblood.
An Anub'ar champion is a combatant.
An Anub'ar crypt fiend is a combatant.
An Anub'ar necromancer is a combatant.
A brown rabbit is a small critter rather than a conversational character.
A wailing Drakkari soul is an undead presence.
Naznik Sureshave is a barber whose welcome advertises grooming and appearance changes, including facial hair, piercings, night elf tattoos, and draenei horns and tendrils.
Pulik Swiftsnip is a barber whose welcome advertises grooming and appearance changes, including piercings, tusks, horns, and undead features.
Ghostly Skull is a non-combat pet.
Animated Bones, an undead creature.
An Apothecary bat-rider controller.
Kunz Jr. is a humanoid.
An undead shade, distinguished by its frozen nature.
The Defender of the Light is identified with the Argent Dawn. In combat, it uses Heroic Leap, Holy Strike, Holy Wrath and Uppercut; when a friendly unit falls below 20% health, it casts Holy Light.

Highlord Tirion Fordring challenges Darion and condemns the hatred and darkness that consumed Arthas, accusing an opponent of betraying the principles his father fought for. He mourns honorable knights slain defending others but urges vigilance rather than forgetting their deaths. He demands that the Lich King answer for his deeds and be prevented from causing further destruction.
Korfax, Champion of the Light, warns that Scourge armies are approaching. In battle, when brought near defeat, he falls unconscious and becomes protected from further attack.
Commander Eligor Dawnbringer is a named, high-ranking combatant. When brought near defeat in battle, he stops fighting, falls unconscious and becomes protected from further attack.

Lord Maxwell Tyrosus urges his brothers and sisters to stand fast, declaring that the Light will prevail, then sharply orders an attack. When brought near defeat in battle, he falls unconscious and becomes protected from further attack.
Leonid Barthalomew the Revered is a named individual. He falls unconscious when nearly defeated.
Nicholas Zverenhoff bears the title of duke and can fall unconscious in combat.
Rayne is a humanoid who can fall unconscious in combat.
Rimblat Earthshatter is a humanoid who can fall unconscious in combat.

This portrayal of the Lich King tells Tirion Fordring that he deliberately sent others to die and regards their lives as meaningless. He boasts of drawing Fordring out of hiding, calls the paladin exposed, and threatens that nothing will save him. He vows that their next meeting will take place away from holy ground.
Impale Target is a combat target that casts a spell.
A Plague Eruptor, an undead creature.
A Coldwraith, an undead creature.
A massive undead creature of flesh.
An undead frozen shade.
Mograine’s undead mount.
Koltira Deathweaver is a named combatant who fights with Death Coil.
Thassarian is a named combatant who fights with Death Coil and Icy Touch.
An undead mount for a death knight.
Orbaz Bloodbane is a named humanoid combatant who uses Blood Strike and Icy Touch in combat.
A warrior of the Frozen Wastes is a humanoid combatant. It casts Cleave in combat and Emerge.
Carrion Beetle is a creature named for a beetle.
Frigid Bones is a humanoid creature.
An Anub'ar Darter is a humanoid creature that uses Dart in combat.
An Anub'ar Assassin is a humanoid creature.
A helper called a Disciple of the Unholy Bunny.
An Anub'ar guardian: a combatant that uses Sunder Armor in combat.

Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the Ashbringer, treasures his home and family. He tells Darion Mograine that he is barely old enough to hold a sword and fears losing him against Lordaeron’s undead hordes. He foresees his son one day wielding the Ashbringer to bring justice and pride to their people, but insists that day has not yet come.

This portrayal of Darion Mograine eagerly seeks to fight the undead beside his father. He welcomes his father’s return after a long absence, says he can no longer sit idle, and declares that he would rather die standing against the undead legions with him. His affectionate greeting includes an embrace.
A poisonous skitterer, a beast.
An undead Lesser Shadow Construct.

The Image of Arthas praises a sacrifice as proof of obedience, declares its recipient worthy of a charge, and names that person Svala Sorrowgrave. He commands the destruction of uninvited guests as a first test. His address emphasizes obedience and worthiness through service.

A corrupted Scarlet Onslaught creature, this combatant uses Flesh Rip in combat.

Landgren's Soul resists a monster's attempt to influence him, first refusing to disclose information before breaking and agreeing to reveal where “he” is. His replies show resistance turning to capitulation under pressure.
A Drakkari Elemental gathers its mojo and surges into battle. When it falls, its remnants seep into the ground and a nearby altar glows faintly, tying its destruction to the surrounding ritual.
An infectious undead ghoul.

Dreadlord Mal'Ganis commands the Onslaught and vows revenge on the Lich King and the player. He says he must gather strength on his homeworld, describes his former shell as weak, and declares himself eternal.

Tormar Frostgut is the target of Gino’s planned assault at Frostgut’s Altar, deep in a cave intended for demolition. Gino wants him killed after explosives are planted, followed by a quick escape. Tormar greets visitors as delicious morsels and taunts them with the prospect of using their bombs to cook them.

She can carry a rider and work a trail; during the pursuit she signals when the group is spotted and when she has found the thief's hiding place. Her hunter trusts her tracking and leaves the confrontation to her companion.

General Lightsbane is an undead death knight serving the Lich King and overseeing weapon production within the Shadow Vault. His enemies regard him as too tightly bound to the Lich King’s will to turn except under extraordinary circumstances, and seek his defeat to claim the vault. He dismisses the intruder disrupting his work as an easy opponent.

Gymer is King of the Storm Giants. He boasts of crushing opponents beneath his enormous boots and invokes storms and lightning to guide his fury. In farewell, he thanks a friend for what they have done, promises never to forget it, and hopes they will meet again under better circumstances.
Herbalism Flower.
